- Familiar with accounting, financial statement analysis, and financial modeling is a plus, but not required

- Prior experience with Python is a plus, but not required

- Available to start working full-time in August 2028

postings.title: Hardware Engineer (FPGA/ASIC)
postings.description:
About the Position

Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you are paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.

In this internship, you'll learn how we use tools to make programming faster, more pleasant, and more reliable. We apply these same principles to our hardware engineering work, and we're looking for people who are interested in using programming language technology to improve the process of designing, testing, and validating hardware designs. We use Hardcaml, an OCaml library for succinctly describing hardware in RTL. Hardcaml is tightly integrated into our development environment, so you'll also gain lots of exposure to the libraries and tools that are foundational to our internal systems. No previous knowledge of Hardcaml is required.

The hardware team at Jane Street works on both FPGA and ASIC designs. Depending on your background and experience, we'll craft a project that gives you exposure to our shared Hardcaml tech stack, as well as targeting an FPGA or ASIC platform.

During the program, you'll dive deep on one project, mentored closely by the full-time employees who helped design it. Some intern projects consider big-picture questions that we're still trying to figure out, while others involve building something new. Your mentors will help you gain a better understanding of the wide range of problems we solve every day. We expect interns to build hardware applications from concept to a working design; your projects will predominantly involve OCaml & Hardcaml, for both RTL design and testing/integration.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process, meet some of our newest hires, or check out our OCaml All The Way Down talk and Programmable Hardware podcast episode. You can also learn more about Jane Street’s internship programme here.

About You

We don't expect you to have a background in finance, OCaml, functional programming, or any other specific field— we're looking for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Comfortable with a software programming language

- Experienced with a Hardware Description (or Construction) language (VHDL, Verilog, Chisel, Pymtl, or other), for both writing and testing hardware designs

- Experienced working with FPGA or ASIC vendor tools - Vivado or Quartus for FPGAs, Genus or Innovus for ASICs

- Experienced with building a working hardware project (either FPGA or ASIC) through an academic, professional, or personal project

- Interested in learning how to use FPGAs or ASICs in the context of networking

- Fluent in English

postings.title: HR Partner
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for an HR Partner to support our team in New York in a broad range of strategic and operational responsibilities.

Your ability to pivot from strategic thinking to practical implementation and back will be critical. On a given day, you might serve as a resource for employees to resolve issues, hold long-term strategic discussions with leaders, coach new managers on employee relations issues, help design and improve our people processes (e.g., performance management), and dig into data. 

As you work alongside other HR Partners to support colleagues, you will also be a key member of our global HR team. Our HR team is an extremely dedicated group of people across our New York, London, and Hong Kong offices who enjoy working collaboratively to keep Jane Street an excellent place to work. 

You will lend your expertise to inform strategy on issues related to firm growth, performance feedback, career and leadership development. There will also be opportunities to collaborate on initiatives on a global scale and refine the role to meet the evolving needs of the firm over time. 

Jane Street is a challenging, dynamic place to work with smart and intellectually curious people. Our organizational structure is flat with few titles, and you will have the opportunity to adapt your deep experience in a broad array of human resources disciplines to our distinctive work culture. 

About You 

- Have a bachelor's degree and around 10 years of experience in HR, including 5+ years in an HR Business Partner role

- Mature and professional; you handle information with sensitivity and care

- A flexible team player who is comfortable both managing and doing the work yourself

- Positive and approachable; you stay composed, prepared, and balanced in all interactions 

- Have a strong understanding of HR best practices; you may not have all the answers, but you know where to find them

- Excellent written and spoken communicator; you choose words thoughtfully

postings.description:
About the Position

As an Infrastructure Automation Specialist, you will be interfacing with various Infrastructure groups locally and globally to help manage the processes and tools used within and between such groups, as well as those used to interact with external parties. You will become familiar with both the broad flow of the trading/settlement cycle as well as the regulatory and operational considerations of each step. As you gain in-depth understanding of the day-to-day operations of each Infrastructure team, you will dedicate an increasing amount of time to the coding and development functions, as well as helping these groups monitor and update complex spreadsheets, optimize existing processes and develop new tools.

postings.title: IT Operations Engineer
postings.description:
About the Position

If you are imagining a daily routine that involves making copies and watching as someone turns a computer off and back on, think again: this is not your typical IT internship. Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you'll be paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.

We will train you as if you're joining our full-time team of IT Operations Engineers who are responsible for the support, configuration and operation of multiple systems across all of our technology stacks, including desktop engineering, network and various application platforms. You will help in a hands-on capacity as we make improvements to our office environment. This can include: responding to technology support requests, building and configuring Windows and Linux devices, supporting our Windows domain infrastructure, monitoring and supporting systems and helping with projects to optimize the way we work using tools like PowerShell.

Our IT interns are friendly and collaborative problem-solvers who enjoy helping people. They are able to troubleshoot in real time and engage with our end users, and are comfortable asking questions and admitting to mistakes. Our internships provide a great introduction to Jane Street and how we think about and solve problems across all teams. Often, successful interns have been invited to return for a full-time position after graduation.

Learn more about Jane Street’s internship program here.

About You

If you've never thought about a career in finance, you're in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you'll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Knowledgeable of computer hardware components and how they interact with each other

- Familiar with the Windows operating system

- Interested in learning about networking, programming or system administration

- Eager to help people and solve problems; able to communicate clearly and respectfully

- A reliable team player with a "no job too small" attitude

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment

- Humble and unafraid to ask questions and admit mistakes

- Able to deconstruct technical problems, and willing to take a hands-on approach to gain experience in diagnosing, troubleshooting and resolving technical issues at the desktop, server and network levels

- Able to develop and maintain technical documentation

- Some familiarity (either personal, academic, or professional) with a scripting language, such as PowerShell or Bash, is a plus 

- Fluent in English

postings.title: Linux Engineer
postings.description:
About the Position

We're looking for Linux Engineers to join the team that maintains the critical infrastructure underlying the rest of Jane Street's technology. It's a broad role, and no two Linux Engineers look exactly alike. Our work spans on-prem and cloud infrastructure, every major pillar (compute, storage, networking), and every layer of the stack from the physical hardware to workload orchestration. You should expect to work in some (but not necessarily all) of these areas, and to go genuinely deep in a few.

That might mean:

- Building the in-house tools and systems that make up our platform, or integrating mainstream (often open-source) technologies so they feel native to our infrastructure

- Acting as one of the firm's Linux experts, and teaching other engineers specialist skills like systems debugging

- Automating our own work, because it makes us faster and more reliable (and we think it's fun)

- Diagnosing and resolving production issues in real time, often under time pressure

- Carrying out scheduled changes to the platform, like upgrades, migrations, capacity changes, and rollouts, planned meticulously and executed carefully

The problem space runs from the physical to the abstract: datacenter provisioning and orchestration, kernels and drivers delivered through Nix and RPMs, production and research storage at scale, cloud that integrates cleanly with our on-prem platform, and, in partnership with our IT and Network Engineering colleagues, Linux desktops and how our hosts participate in the network.

We see Linux Engineering and Software Engineering as two ends of a spectrum, and plenty of people could do either job well. Linux Engineering is likely the better fit if you treat Linux itself as your problem space: you like working close to the operating system, you want to look after production infrastructure, and you're happy spending more of your time in a consulting capacity than a typical developer would. (Compared with kernel development, the emphasis flips: you'd rarely develop the kernel itself, though targeted patches happen, and you'd spend far more time running production infrastructure.) We're hiring for both roles and are happy to advise you on which might fit best.

We don't expect you to come in with deep experience; we're happy to hire smart problem-solvers and teach them what they need to know. But the job leans much more toward engineering than a traditional operations role: relentless automation instead of manual toil, and a large body of in-house technology rather than only off-the-shelf tools. You'll build systems, not just operate them.

About You

We don't expect you to have a background in finance or any other specific field - we're looking for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Knowledgeable about operating system fundamentals, computer architecture, and systems programming concepts like sockets, virtual memory, and the process life cycle

- Able to understand network protocols at a basic level

- Programming experience in any language (functional languages a plus)

- Fluency in English required

postings.title: Linux Engineer
postings.description:
About the Position

We're looking for Linux Engineers to join the team that maintains the critical infrastructure underlying the rest of Jane Street's technology. It's a broad role, and no two Linux Engineers look exactly alike. Our work spans on-prem and cloud infrastructure, every major pillar (compute, storage, networking), and every layer of the stack from the physical hardware to workload orchestration. You should expect to work in some (but not necessarily all) of these areas, and to go genuinely deep in a few.

That might mean:

- Building the in-house tools and systems that make up our platform, or integrating mainstream (often open-source) technologies so they feel native to our infrastructure

- Acting as one of the firm's Linux experts, and teaching other engineers specialist skills like systems debugging

- Automating our own work, because it makes us faster and more reliable (and we think it's fun)

- Diagnosing and resolving production issues in real time, often under time pressure

- Carrying out scheduled changes to the platform, like upgrades, migrations, capacity changes, and rollouts, planned meticulously and executed carefully

The problem space runs from the physical to the abstract: datacenter provisioning and orchestration, kernels and drivers delivered through Nix and RPMs, production and research storage at scale, cloud that integrates cleanly with our on-prem platform, and, in partnership with our IT and Network Engineering colleagues, Linux desktops and how our hosts participate in the network.

We see Linux Engineering and Software Engineering as two ends of a spectrum, and plenty of people could do either job well. Linux Engineering is likely the better fit if you treat Linux itself as your problem space: you like working close to the operating system, you want to look after production infrastructure, and you're happy spending more of your time in a consulting capacity than a typical developer would. (Compared with kernel development, the emphasis flips: you'd rarely develop the kernel itself, though targeted patches happen, and you'd spend far more time running production infrastructure.) We're hiring for both roles and are happy to advise you on which might fit best.

We don't expect you to come in with deep experience; we're happy to hire smart problem-solvers and teach them what they need to know. But the job leans much more toward engineering than a traditional operations role: relentless automation instead of manual toil, and a large body of in-house technology rather than only off-the-shelf tools. You'll build systems, not just operate them.

About You

We don't expect you to have a background in finance or any other specific field - we're looking for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Knowledgeable about operating system fundamentals, computer architecture, and systems programming concepts like sockets, virtual memory, and the process life cycle

- Able to understand network protocols at a basic level

- Comfortable at the command line of a Linux machine (whether from coursework, side projects, or time spent administering a campus computer lab) and fluent in basic introspection and troubleshooting: system health, individual processes, logs

- Someone who solves problems by writing code (in any language) and cares about robust software engineering

- Intellectually curious, collaborative, humble, and eager to learn (including from mistakes)

- A strong communicator

- Fluent in English 

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

We are seeking a leader for our growing team of Linux Engineers.

Members of this group, managers and individual contributors alike, are hard-working Systems Engineers, Administrators, and Programmers, tasked with maintaining and improving the platform that powers Jane Street's production trading systems. (Find out more about the Linux Engineer role here).

We expect managers to come in and lead by example. As well as supporting their teams, the ideal candidate will be excited to start off as an individual contributor, establish a fundamental understanding of Jane Street's technical environment, and gradually grow into a management role.

postings.title: Low-Latency Engineer
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for a Software Engineer with experience in high-performance, low latency systems. You’ll work closely with our quantitative researchers and developers, taking a holistic approach to design and optimize our fast-trading systems.

We build systems primarily in OCaml with only small amounts of C and C++, but you don’t need any experience with OCaml in particular (we can teach it to you) or knowledge of the financial markets. The most important qualification is experience with low level systems programming and optimization, whether it is in C, C++, or any other language. 

About You

- Experience with low level systems programming and optimization, and working on network applications that require extremely low latency and high throughput

- Can understand, interpret, and improve application performance through hardware performance counters and other profiling tools

- Has a thorough understanding of modern computer architecture and can talk to others about it; for example, can you describe modern x86 AMD and Intel cache hierarchies?

- Some experience with fast-packet processing in user space and common kernel-bypass implementations would be ideal (such as Solarflare OpenOnload/TCPDirect/ef_vi, Exablaze, InfiniBand verbs, DPDK)

- Experience working around the performance challenges of languages with a managed runtime (such as Java or C#) and familiarity with a typed functional language are a plus

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Machine Learning Compiler Engineer
postings.description:
About the position

We’re looking for compiler engineers to join a new ML Compilers Team at Jane Street. 

Machine learning is a critical pillar of our global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction. Our ML team is full of people with a shared love for the craft of software engineering, and for designing APIs and systems that are delightful to use.

ML compilers let us quickly turn research ideas and novel architectures into high-throughput training jobs and low-latency inference. To get the most out of our hardware resources and enable rapid model development and deployment, we are working to understand and improve the current ML compiler technologies and explore where it makes sense to build our own solutions. In this role, you would shape the development of our compiler stack.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in.

About you

The ideal candidate has worked on an ML compiler in the past, but non-ML compiler experience is also valuable. Experience with any part of the stack is fine, be it high-level ML frameworks (PyTorch, Jax, TensorFlow), graph compilers (Inductor, XLA, TVM) or kernel DSLs (Triton, Helion, cuTile). postings.title: Machine Learning Performance Engineer
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
We are looking for an engineer with experience in low-level systems programming and optimization to join our growing ML team. 

Machine learning is a critical pillar of Jane Street's global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction.

Your part here is optimizing the performance of our models – both training and inference. We care about efficient large-scale training, low-latency inference in real-time systems, and high-throughput inference in research. Part of this is improving straightforward CUDA, but the interesting part needs a whole-systems approach, including storage systems, networking, and host- and GPU-level considerations. Zooming in, we also want to ensure our platform makes sense even at the lowest level – is all that throughput actually goodput? Does loading that vector from the L2 cache really take that long?

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. 

There’s no fixed set of skills, but here are some of the things we’re looking for:

- An understanding of modern ML techniques and toolsets

- The experience and systems knowledge required to debug a training run’s performance end to end

- Low-level GPU knowledge of PTX, SASS, warps, cooperative groups, Tensor Cores, and the memory hierarchy

- Debugging and optimization experience using tools like CUDA GDB, NSight Systems, NSight Compute

- Library knowledge of Triton, CUTLASS, CUB, Thrust, cuDNN, and cuBLAS

- Intuition about the latency and throughput characteristics of CUDA graph launch, tensor core arithmetic, warp-level synchronization, and asynchronous memory loads

- Background in Infiniband, RoCE, GPUDirect, PXN, rail optimization, and NVLink, and how to use these networking technologies to link up GPU clusters

- An understanding of the collective algorithms supporting distributed GPU training in NCCL or MPI

- An inventive approach and the willingness to ask hard questions about whether we're taking the right approaches and using the right tools

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Machine Learning Research Engineer
postings.description:
We are looking for a Research Engineer with robust experience in machine learning and strong mathematical foundations to join our growing ML team and to help drive the direction of our ML platform.

Machine learning is a critical pillar of Jane Street's global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction. Our ML team is full of people with a shared love for the craft of software engineering, and for designing APIs and systems that are delightful to use. 

We’ll rely on your in-depth knowledge of the ML ecosystem and understanding of varying approaches - whether it’s neural networks, random forests, gradient-boosted trees or sophisticated ensemble methods - to aid decision-making so we apply the right tool for the problem at hand. Your work will also focus on enhancing research workflows to tighten our feedback cycles. Successful ML Research Engineers will be able to understand the mechanics behind various modelling techniques, while also being able to break down the mathematics behind them. We’re looking for people who can be a true bridge between research and engineering, and can help us push forward the frontier of our model capabilities at all points of the stack. This could involve enabling a new scale in our technology stack, sitting on a team of Researchers to rapidly prototype a new research idea, or building workflow APIs that support a wide range of use cases.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. While there isn’t a fixed list of qualifications we’re looking for, if you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. 

We're looking for someone with:

- Experience building and maintaining training and inference infrastructure, with an understanding of what it takes to move from concept to production

- A strong mathematical background; Good candidates will be excited about things like optimisation theory, regularisation techniques, linear algebra and the like

- A passion for keeping up with the state of the art, whether that means diving into academic papers, experimenting with the latest hardware or reading the source of a new machine learning package

- A proven ability to create and maintain an organised research codebase that produces robust, reproducible results while maintaining ease of use

- Expertise wrangling an ML framework – we're fans of PyTorch, but we'd also love to learn what you know about Jax, TensorFlow or others

- An inventive approach and the willingness to ask hard questions about whether we're taking the right approaches and using the right tools

- Fluent in English

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Machine Learning Researcher
postings.description:
About the Position

Our goals are to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street as a Machine Learning Researcher while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll work side by side with experienced ML Researchers on projects that we've selected for their combination of novel ML ideas and relevance to real-world systematic trading strategies. You'll learn how we think about markets through challenging classes and activities, and practice using established methods alongside our own unique twists to train practical models.

At Jane Street, the lines between research, technology, and trading are intentionally blurry, and you’ll have access to petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Trading poses unusual challenges—large models and nonstationary datasets in a competitive multi-agent environment—that force us to search for novel techniques.

You'll spend the bulk of your internship working closely with full-time machine learning researchers on projects drawn from their own work. You might conduct an end-to-end study of an unexplored dataset, try a new modelling paradigm for a thorny problem, or consider blue-sky approaches that we're still trying to figure out. The problems we work on rarely have clean, definitive answers, and they often require insights from colleagues across the firm with different areas of expertise. Depending on the day, you might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging training issues, or analysing the predictions your model makes.

Note that given the IP-sensitive nature of machine learning research at Jane Street, it is unlikely that any research findings associated with the internship will be suitable for outside academic publication.

About you

If you've never thought about a career in finance, you're in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you'll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- An undergraduate, PhD student, or postdoc with practical experience working on ML problems

- Interested in applying logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems

- Curious about the machine learning landscape and excited to apply state-of-the-art techniques drawn from many problem domains

- Fluent with a versatile set of models and tricks

- Able to rapidly implement and iterate on your ideas in Python and your favourite ML framework

- Eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things

- Fluent in English

If you'd like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team. Learn more about Jane Street's internship program here.

We’re looking for smart and curious individuals to join our growing team and drive our ML work.

On our Machine Learning team, you'll build the deep learning models that power our trading strategies, supported by our rapidly growing computing cluster with tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Trading poses unusual challenges—large models and nonstationary datasets in a competitive multi-agent environment—that force us to search for novel techniques. 

At Jane Street, our researchers, engineers, and traders sit a few feet away from each other and work together to train models, architect systems, and run trading strategies. Depending on the day, we might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging distributed training performance, or studying how our model likes to trade in production.

postings.title: Machine Learning Researcher
postings.description:
About the position

Our goals are to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street as a Machine Learning Researcher while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll work side by side with experienced ML Researchers on projects that we've selected for their combination of novel ML ideas and relevance to real-world systematic trading strategies. You'll learn how we think about markets through challenging classes and activities, and practice using established methods alongside our own unique twists to train practical models.

At Jane Street, the lines between research, technology, and trading are intentionally blurry, and you’ll have access to petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Trading poses unusual challenges—large models and nonstationary datasets in a competitive multi-agent environment—that force us to search for novel techniques.

You'll spend the bulk of your internship working closely with full-time machine learning researchers on projects drawn from their own work. You might conduct an end-to-end study of an unexplored dataset, try a new modeling paradigm for a thorny problem, or consider blue-sky approaches that we're still trying to figure out. The problems we work on rarely have clean, definitive answers, and they often require insights from colleagues across the firm with different areas of expertise. Depending on the day, you might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging training issues, or analyzing the predictions your model makes.

Note that given the IP-sensitive nature of machine learning research at Jane Street, it is unlikely that any research findings associated with the internship will be suitable for outside academic publication.

About you

If you've never thought about a career in finance, you're in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you'll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- An undergraduate, PhD student, or postdoc with practical experience working on ML problems

- Interested in applying logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems

- Curious about the machine learning landscape and excited to apply state-of-the-art techniques drawn from many problem domains

- Fluent with a versatile set of models and tricks

- Able to rapidly implement and iterate on your ideas in Python and your favorite ML framework

- Eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things

- Fluent in English

If you'd like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team. Learn more about Jane Street's internship program here.

Please note: Jane Street will provide flights to and from Hong Kong, and accommodation throughout the entirety of the program.

postings.title: Network Analyst
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for a Network Analyst who can provide support as our team builds automation and DevOps-driven solutions – encouraging creativity in leveraging AI wherever possible. 

Our global network infrastructure underpins a variety of traffic profiles, from fast-paced trading to broader internet connectivity. You’ll partner with our senior engineers and developers across the firm to enhance existing workflows, streamline processes and ensure that our network remains stable, secure and adaptable. 

We seek candidates who enjoy solving complex problems and want to develop expertise in both operations and creative infrastructure engineering. A typical day in this role includes:

- Providing hands-on support to diagnose and resolve network issues across LAN, WAN and colocation environments

- Working with project managers on site expansions, new market data feeds and connections to third-party services

- Maintaining and improving our monitoring and alert systems, with a strong emphasis on automation, AI integration and DevOps practices

- Using scripting or development tools to reduce manual tasks, enhance network visibility and explore innovative AI-driven solutions

This position is an exciting chance to be directly mentored by experienced network engineers with cutting-edge hardware, protocols and DevOps tools. Your daily support will have a direct impact on our operational excellence and your contributions to automation, AI integration and tooling will define the future of our network. 

About You

- Experienced with operating and troubleshooting LAN/WAN networks

- Familiar with common routing and switching protocols (e.g., OSPF, BGP, PIM-SM)

- Able to debug transport protocols (TCP/UDP)

- Comfortable in Linux environments and have some programming or scripting knowledge

- Enthusiastic about automation (for instance, using Python or similar tools) to simplify network operations, and open to AI-powered optimisations

- Eager to learn and adapt, creative and open to feedback

- Strong communicator; ready to interface with global teams and internal stakeholders

- Organised and flexible, able to balance day-to-day support with longer-term projects

- Have a collaborative spirit and thrive in a hands-on, team-driven environment

- Fluent in English

- Having knowledge or hands-on experience with overlay networks such as EVPN or VxLAN is a plus

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Network Engineer
postings.description:
About the position

Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you are paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done.

As a Network Engineer intern, you’ll work with full-timers to learn how we maintain and improve a critical piece of infrastructure underlying our firm’s technology. Our numerous distributed systems are built on a reliable, multi-vendor network infrastructure that supports all traffic profiles from trading to internet connectivity.

On any given day, we might be: 

- Working on cross-team projects such as site expansions and new colocation builds

- Debugging routing protocols

- Provisioning new market data feeds and connections to third parties

- Automating support tasks and improving the team's ability to monitor the network

You’ll have a unique opportunity to see how our team interacts with several groups to build solutions that work on a firm-wide scale. We automate as much of our work as we can because we find that automation reduces our error rate and overall workload—plus, we think it's fun.

Your internship project might consider big-picture questions that we’re still trying to figure out, or involve building something new. Your mentors will help you understand the range of problems we solve every day, from finding new and interesting ways to resolve production issues quickly, to performing comprehensive root-cause analyses and integrating clean and robust long-term fixes.

Learn more about Jane Street’s internship program here.

About you

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Able to understand network protocols (ARP, BGP, OSPF) at a basic level

- Knowledgeable of operating system fundamentals and computer architecture

- A strong programmer who can demonstrate high potential and an aptitude for learning

- Intellectually curious, collaborative, and eager to learn

- Humble and unafraid to ask questions and admit mistakes

- A strong communicator

- Comfortable at the command line of a *nix machine

- Fluent in English

postings.title: Network Engineer, Security
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for an experienced Network Engineer to join our Network Security team to help us run, scale, and continuously improve our network security infrastructure through hands-on operations, design, and implementation. The ideal candidate will have strong networking fundamentals and experience with security appliances such as firewalls and proxy.

Jane Street’s numerous distributed systems are built on an agile, reliable, multi-vendor network infrastructure that supports all traffic profiles, from trading to internet connectivity. Supporting such a large multi-function network requires advanced tooling for monitoring and automation. 

Strong communication and interpersonal skills will be needed to collaborate with colleagues across the firm globally. You will find and resolve issues, plan and execute deployments, and improve systems where possible. We’ll also look to leverage your advanced networking skills and security knowledge to: 

- Work closely with our Network Engineering team on the design and deployment of security perimeter and adjacent network infrastructure

- Manage and continuously evolve network segmentation, DMZ, and other aspects of network security

- Evaluate and lab test new platforms for our network security infrastructure

- Collaborate with our Cybersecurity team on the detection and mitigation of threats and vulnerabilities on our network

- Interface with application owners and traders to enable business workflows securely

- Proactively enhance support by improving network infrastructure observability and scripting, and communicating requirements to our software engineers

- Improve our network security processes and documentation

A holistic approach to system design is critical for this role. Our broader Networking team prioritizes flexibility, compatibility, and efficiency when crafting solutions, all while seeking ongoing buy-in and feedback from users across the firm. Our firm’s culture prizes intellectual humility, openness, and continuous improvement, which translates directly to the daily work of this team. We’re all partners working toward shared goals and are always looking for the next best idea that will make our work stronger. 

Your strong communication skills and analytical thinking will be invaluable as we support the daily work of our colleagues and keep our systems operating at the highest standard.

About You

- Have 7+ years of experience operating and deploying network infrastructure

- Experienced with routing and network protocols (OSPF, BGP, PIM-SM)

- Experienced with troubleshooting transport protocols (TCP/UDP)

- Have a strong understanding of firewall hardware architecture, performance metrics, and functional components

- Experienced with firewall configuration and troubleshooting

- Understand Public Key Infrastructure and related technologies

- Understand modern encryption techniques

- Have a high capacity to learn; we are interested in how you think, not just what you know

- Able to context-switch, while still being able to prioritize and organize your stack 

- Ideally have experience with overlay networks (EVPN, VxLAN)

- A flexible and reliable team player who enjoys working in a collaborative environment

- Preferably have proficiency in a programming language

- Fluency in English required

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Operations Specialist
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for a proactive, enthusiastic problem-solver to join our Operations team. We sit at the heart of Jane Street’s trading, ensuring that assets, information, and ideas flow smoothly and efficiently both within the firm and between us and the outside world.

As our trading grows in scale and complexity, we have to continually rethink and improve the way we work. That’s where this role comes in. 

To start, you'll be embedded within one of our Operations teams, learning the day-to-day work alongside your colleagues—running the processes, understanding the products, building real context for how things get done and why. 

Over time, your focus will shift toward making that work better. That might mean redesigning how a reconciliation is done, removing handoffs between teams, imagining how tools and systems could work better, or applying AI where it helps. You'll look for the changes that would make the biggest difference, help build them, and see them through to adoption.

As you build context and a track record, you'll be pulled into problems in other Operations teams as well, and the balance will tip toward the process-improvement side of the work. The best people in this role end up with a view of Operations that few others have.

We expect this role to evolve over time, and we're looking for someone who's energized by that and embraces it.

About You

- Have a bachelor's degree and 2+ years of experience in operations, engineering, analytics, consulting, or a related field

- Notice inefficiencies and gaps in teams, tools, and processes, and take the initiative to improve them

- Pragmatic about problem-solving and think carefully about which solution best fits your problem (e.g., spreadsheets, scripts, AI)

- Comfortable digging into complex ideas and making them clear for others

- Self-starter and able to set your own direction in ambiguous situations

- Humble about what you know and don’t know, and not afraid to ask questions

- Technical skills are a plus but not a requirement—we care more about how you think than what you can build

You don't need to match every line but if most of this resonates, we'd love to hear from you. 

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: OTC Derivatives Reporting Specialist
postings.description:
About the position

We’re looking for an experienced OTC Derivatives Reporting Specialist to help our Legal and Compliance team build and operate reliable swap reporting across APAC, with a particular focus on Singapore and Hong Kong.

You’ll work closely with our internal Trading, Operations and Legal and Compliance teams, and our software engineers, to turn reporting requirements into working systems. This is a hands-on role for someone who understands how swaps are traded, documented, booked and managed throughout their lifecycle, and who enjoys working through the details of how those transactions should be reported.

Additional responsibilities of this role will include:

- Resolving interpretation questions with your Legal and Compliance colleagues, then translating requirements into clear, field-level mappings–from internal bookings and lifecycle events to reporting schemas

- Working with software engineers to specify source data, transformation logic, and exception handling, and testing implementations to ensure reports are complete and accurate

- Understanding where internal booking representations differ from the transactions and events that need to be reported, and identifying reporting challenges caused by booking conventions, missing data or product complexity

- Investigating rejected submissions, reconciliation breaks, and incorrect or missing reports; tracing issues to their root causes; and helping implement corrections and controls to prevent recurrence

- Engaging early on new products and trading flows to explain reporting requirements and to find practical ways to support trading while meeting regulatory obligations

- Keeping pace with regulatory and technical changes, maintaining clear documentation, and working with reporting providers and counterparties to resolve issues

About you

postings.title: OxCaml Educator
postings.description:
About the Position

Jane Street is hard at work building OxCaml, a branch of OCaml with a variety of extensions to support performance engineering. But designing and implementing the language is only half the battle: we need our developers to understand its nuances and program in OxCaml as experts. That's where you come in.

We’re looking for an experienced, skilled educator to help us develop materials and deliver courses to teach engineers at Jane Street how to use OxCaml effectively. You would work broadly across our internal educational programs, from expanding our OCaml Bootcamp for new hires to use OxCaml to developing specific tutorials to level-up experienced developers that need OxCaml's most advanced features.

This is a unique opportunity to work hand-in-hand with a language's designers and implementers to develop its educational component. You would be part of the team within Jane Street building the next generation of OxCaml.

Here’s what we’re looking for:

- We want someone who is a skilled, effective, and experienced teacher. Part of that means being an effective writer and presenter.

- The job demands an understanding of our technology stack, and the best way to build that understanding is by doing. That means we want someone who is good at writing code, and is excited to spend a significant fraction of their time doing so.

- Part of the job is going to be directly teaching and developing curricula. But an equally important part is helping other people involved in teaching grow their skills, so we want someone who is good at mentoring other budding teachers.

postings.title: Production Engineer
postings.description:
About the Position

We are hiring Production Engineers in our Hong Kong and Singapore office. Jane Street Production Engineers are software developers who spend time both developing software and also providing high-quality support for software systems that are critical to Jane Street's trading business.

Many of our Production Engineers are embedded in various software teams; others are in standalone teams. In both situations we work alongside application developers with a common goal of creating and running great software systems. As a firm we are big believers in functional programming, and use OCaml as our primary development language.

Production Engineers play an essential role interacting with a wide variety of departments and functions at Jane Street. We solve real-time issues and make a firm-wide impact. We take ownership of the architecture and design of systems that monitor and support the firm’s trading. We also design and develop the tools that we use, and it feels great to be able to shape these tools and then enjoy the improvements.

If you'd like to learn more, you can read about Production Engineering at Jane Street. 

How is a Production Engineer role different from a generic Software Engineering role?

As Production Engineers:

- We split our time between OCaml software development project work and a support rotation, in which we actively resolve live issues in Jane Street’s critical systems

- We are curious and eager to learn about a number of different systems and how they fit together. This gives us a breadth of knowledge and opportunities to collaborate with many other dev and business teams across the firm

- We spend less time in total coding (due to the support rotation), and are interrupted more often, and we enjoy adding value to Jane Street in this way

- We get satisfaction from helping others, enabling good trades, and getting to the bottom of complex and urgent production issues

About You

We don’t expect you to have a background in functional programming, finance, or any other specific field—we’re looking for smart software developers who enjoy solving interesting problems. We’re more interested in how you think and learn than just what you currently know. You should be:

- A strong programmer with a love for technology; able to write and read code well

- An intellectually curious person who is motivated, collaborative, and eager to learn

- An excellent communicator, able to be clear and calm during production incidents

- Fluent in English

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Programming Language Engineer
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

We're looking for Software Engineers with a background in programming languages to join one of our PL-focused teams at Jane Street.

Programming languages work at Jane Street spans a wide variety of different areas:

- Language design and type systems. Designing language features and stronger type-level guarantees that let our developers express more of what they mean, and catch more mistakes at compile time.

- Compilers and optimization. Investing in optimization, code generation, and backend work that translates directly into measurable speedups across the firm's most performance-sensitive systems.

- Incremental and parallel computation. Building runtimes that can evaluate large, irregular, dynamic computation graphs incrementally and/or parallel across many cores and machines, with first-class attention to scheduling, memory, and resource accounting.

- Support for high-performance computing, including work on tooling, verification techniques, and languages for hardware design, as well as support for programming GPUs and other ML accelerators.

- Domain-specific languages. Designing, implementing, and evolving custom languages that power some of our most important internal platforms.

- Tooling and developer experience. Profilers, debuggers, language servers, IDE integrations, documentation tools, and the surrounding infrastructure that makes a language genuinely pleasant to use at scale.

Some of this work involves working on open-source language implementations, like those of OCaml and Python, and for those areas, a meaningful portion of our work is open-source as well. Some of it involves custom languages and DSLs that we’ve built entirely in-house, some open-source, some purely internal.

We’re looking for people who have:

- Deep experience with—and love for—programming languages. There's no specific checklist; we are interested in people with experience in language design, type systems, compilers, runtimes, or DSL implementation

- Top-notch programming skills

- Strong interpersonal skills. Software engineering at Jane Street is highly collaborative, and we are looking for people who can work effectively in small, close-knit teams

No previous experience with OCaml or functional programming is required.

You only need to submit one application for Programming Language Engineering at Jane Street. We’re excited to evaluate folks for areas across all of these roles, but if you feel like your experience relates best to a more specific area, please indicate that in the notes section of your application.

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Quantitative Researcher
postings.description:
About the Position

We are looking for Quantitative Researchers to help us build models, strategies, and systems that price and trade financial instruments. You’ll work side by side with experienced researchers who are committed to teaching, guiding, and supporting our newest hires, learning how we think about experiment design, dataset generation, time series analysis, feature engineering, and model building for financial datasets.

At Jane Street, our researchers, engineers, and traders sit a few feet away from each other and work together to train models, architect systems, and run trading strategies. We work with petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Depending on the day, we might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging distributed training performance, or studying how our model likes to trade in production.

We don’t believe in “one-size-fits-all” modelling solutions; we are open to and excited about applying all different types of statistical and ML techniques, from linear models to deep learning, depending on what best fits a given problem. The most successful researchers will be driven by a curiosity for how their contributions fit into the larger picture of our trading operations, and how to adapt their findings into actionable strategies.

About You

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. You should be:

- Able to apply logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems

- Intellectually curious; eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things 

- A strong programmer who’s comfortable with Python

- An open-minded thinker and precise communicator who enjoys collaborating with colleagues from a wide range of backgrounds and areas of expertise

- Fluent in English

Most candidates will have experience with data science or machine learning, but ultimately, we’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. PhD or other research experience is a plus.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team.

We don’t believe in “one-size-fits-all” modelling solutions; we are open to and excited about applying all different types of statistical and ML techniques, from linear models to deep learning, depending on what best fits a given problem. The most successful researchers will be driven by a curiosity for how their contributions fit into the larger picture of our trading operations, and how to adapt their findings into actionable strategies.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. You should be:

- Able to apply logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems

- Intellectually curious; eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things 

- A strong programmer who’s comfortable with Python

- An open-minded thinker and precise communicator who enjoys collaborating with colleagues from a wide range of backgrounds and areas of expertise

- Fluent in English

Most candidates will have experience with data science or machine learning, but ultimately, we’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. PhD or other research experience is a plus.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team.

postings.title: Quantitative Trader
postings.description:
About the Position

Our trading is based on our own proprietary models and on busy days we engage in over a million trades. Traders work in teams to seek out and trade on pricing inefficiencies, develop models, manage risk, investigate new products, and push into new business areas. Experienced Traders teach and oversee the less-experienced. New Traders serve as assistants while they learn the ropes, getting increasing responsibility as they demonstrate their ability to handle it.

Technology is at the core of how we approach trading, and we consider ourselves as much a technology company as a trading firm. We use OCaml, a statically-typed functional programming language, as our primary development language, and have the largest team of OCaml Engineers in any industrial setting.

About You

We are looking for people who have a strong quantitative mind and enjoy working collaboratively to solve challenging problems in a practical setting. Prior knowledge of finance or economics is not expected or required. Experience with particular programming languages is also not required, although generally being comfortable programming in your language of choice is a plus. Fluency in English required.

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

Our goals are to give you a real sense of what it's like to work as a Quantitative Trader at Jane Street while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. You'll be paired with experienced quantitative traders who will teach you how to identify market signals, analyze and execute strategies, construct quantitative models, conduct statistical analysis, and build trading intuition.

At Jane Street, the lines between research, technology, and trading are intentionally blurry, and you’ll have access to petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. We don't believe in "one-size-fits-all" modeling solutions; we are open to and excited about applying all different types of statistical and ML techniques, from linear models to deep learning, depending on what best fits a given problem. You'll work closely with two different mentors on projects relating to their day-to-day work, giving you a sense of the variety of problems we solve every day. Past projects have included analyzing new or existing datasets, training predictive models, simulating potential new trading strategies, writing tools that we use in production, and even working to answer big-picture questions we haven't yet figured out.

During the internship, your work is reinforced with intensive classes, workshops, and team-based mock trading sessions. These will expose you to many of the dynamics we observe in real markets, illustrate the role that we play in making markets more efficient, and help build intuition for how we think about both trading and collaborating.

As a quantitative trading intern, you'll also have the opportunity to participate in one "elective" based on your interests. Electives consist of targeted classes and immersive activities, and are designed to give you a deeper and more nuanced look into one of the many aspects of what quantitative trading can look like at Jane Street:

Machine Learning, Modeling, and Data Science

You'll learn how Jane Street applies advanced machine learning and statistical techniques to make models and predictions using large datasets of both real and simulated market data. You'll learn how to train and use a variety of ML models, and gain an understanding of the differences between textbook machine learning and its application to noisy and complex financial data. 

Algorithmic Trading and Market Microstructure

You'll learn the end-to-end process of developing an algorithmic trading strategy. You'll analyze market data to develop a tradable fair value and implement a trading strategy in Python. Your algorithmic strategy will connect directly to simulated markets with different market structures, and you will learn how to optimize your strategy given the unique attributes of each market. You will discover how various market dynamics affect strategy behavior and learn how real-world trading differs from simulation.

Trading Strategy and Scenarios

You’ll be introduced to a rotating set of new trading scenarios inspired by real events on a particular trading desk. You’ll work in teams on multiple mock trading sessions related to each scenario and use the time between sessions to refine your strategies, write recaps, and hear how the story played out in real life from our seasoned full-time traders who lived through it.

About You

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. We’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- A strong quantitative thinker (no specific degree or major is required)

- A clear and effective verbal and written communicator

- Someone who enjoys working collaboratively on a team

- Eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things

A profitable trading strategy is only as strong as the technology it runs on, and we consider ourselves as much a technology company as a trading firm. General programming experience is a plus, but knowing a particular programming language is not required.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team. Learn more about Jane Street’s internship program here.

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Recruiting Coordinator
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the Position

We're looking for several Recruiting Coordinators to join our New York team. We want organized, proactive go-getters who are excited to learn and grow on a collaborative team, and care as deeply as we do about getting the little things right and maintaining a warm, welcoming, people-first approach to recruiting. While you should have some professional experience, no prior recruiting experience is required — we can teach you what you need to know.

We're hiring for a few different openings across a range of disciplines on the team. Below is an idea of the focus areas you might be asked to support:

- Campus, Early Careers Partnerships and Initiatives: Supporting our campus recruitment strategy, including engagement and communications with prospective candidates, external partnership relationships, planning and executing recruitment events and programs, representing us at these events, and managing job and event postings. This area involves regular travel. 

- Campus Infrastructure Recruiting: Supporting our campus pipelines for infrastructure roles, including coordinating interviews, managing candidate logistics and communications, and supporting related recruitment events. 

- Experienced Hire, Non-Technology: Supporting lateral hiring for our Infrastructure and Trading teams, including scheduling interviews, managing recruiting calendars, coordinating live interviews, and keeping our applicant tracking system up to date.

- Experienced Hire, Technology: Supporting lateral hiring for our software engineering and other technical roles, including scheduling phone screens and on-sites, managing calendars, and coordinating live interviews.

Our Recruiting team has developed a dynamic strategy and engaging interview process to find and hire some of the best talent from all corners of the world. Your ability to get the details right and create positive connections with our candidates will make you a valuable addition to all aspects of the team.

About You

- Have 1-3 years of professional experience (recruiting, HR, or operations experience is a plus but not required)

- Highly organized with excellent attention to detail; you appreciate how much it matters to get the little things right

- A self-starter who can manage competing priorities and who is comfortable in a fast-paced environment with frequent context-switching

- A clear communicator who can work across teams and respond to a range of stakeholders, including colleagues, candidates, search firms, and external partners

- Humble about what you do and don't know; not afraid to ask for help and eager to ask questions and seek feedback

- A flexible team player with a positive attitude who adapts quickly to changes

- Willing and able to learn new recruiting systems and tools

- Comfortable using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) to work more efficiently

- Having some technical comfort is a plus across all the areas we’re hiring for, and is especially relevant for the Operations track (e.g., building reports, navigating spreadsheets, working with structured data, picking up internal tooling)

- Having experience with tools like Greenhouse, Workday Recruiting, Gem, Jira, or Tableau is a plus

- No financial industry experience is required

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.description:
About the position

We are looking for a Recruiting Coordinator to support our experienced hire team as we identify, interview and hire experienced technology professionals in our Asia offices. We want an organised, proactive go-getter who is excited to learn and grow on a collaborative team, and who cares as deeply as we do about getting the little things right and maintaining a warm, welcoming and people-first approach to recruiting. 

You'll work alongside our seasoned team to learn how we create an incredible candidate experience from start to finish. We will train you in both our day-to-day candidate coordination and the strategy behind our approach. 

Your daily work will focus on our technology teams, and will involve keeping our applicant tracking system updated, scheduling interviews, managing our recruiting calendars, coordinating live interviews as they happen and helping us manage some of our other recruiting tools and platforms.

Our Recruiting team has developed a dynamic strategy and engaging interview process to find and hire some of the best talent from all corners of the world. Your ability to get the details right and create positive connections with our candidates will make you a valuable addition to all aspects of the team.

About you

- Have 0-3 years of professional experience (recruiting, HR or operations experience is a plus but not required)

- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail; you appreciate how much it matters to get the little things right

- A self-starter who can manage competing priorities and who is comfortable in a fast-paced environment with frequent context-switching

- A clear communicator who can work across teams and respond to a range of stakeholders, including colleagues, candidates, search firms and external partners

- Humble about what you do and don't know; not afraid to ask for help and eager to ask questions and seek feedback

- A flexible team player with a positive attitude who adapts quickly to changes

- Willing and able to learn new recruiting systems and tools

- Comfortable using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) to work more efficiently

- Having experience with tools like Greenhouse, Workday Recruiting, Gem, Jira or Tableau is a plus

- No financial industry experience is required

- Fluent in English

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com

postings.title: Recruiting Operations Specialist
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the position

We are looking for a Recruiting Operations Specialist to help us optimize our global recruiting processes, support our systems, and manage key projects. You will be based in our New York office, while also providing crucial support for our European and Asian offices.

Your project management skills and technical aptitude will help us maintain our high standards for hiring exceptional talent. Additional responsibilities of the role will include:

- Mastering our recruiting tech stack, troubleshooting issues, and providing time zone-specific coverage for global offices

- Documenting workflows, identifying inefficiencies, and implementing solutions to reduce operational friction

- Driving recruiting initiatives from planning to execution, and maintaining clear communication with stakeholders

- Building and maintaining automations, scripts and lightweight internal tools that make recruiting workflows faster and more reliable

- Collaborating with internal teams on improving existing recruiting tools and translating user needs into requirements

- Maintaining data integrity, creating reports on key metrics, and offering data-driven recommendations

About you

- Have 4-8 years of relevant experience

- Experienced with recruiting tools and technologies

- Highly organized with strong project management skills

- A systematic thinker with experience documenting complex processes

- A self-sufficient problem solver who is comfortable with ambiguity

- Comfortable querying and analyzing data and drawing conclusions from it

- Have experience developing tools in partnership with engineering and product teams is a plus

- Experienced working on multi-disciplinary recruiting teams or in multi-office, high-growth environments is a plus but not required

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

postings.title: Regulatory Exam Manager
postings.location: New York, New York, United States
postings.description:
About the position

We’re looking for a Regulatory Exam Manager to join our Legal and Compliance team in New York. In this role, you’ll oversee our response to regulatory examinations from start to finish.

You’ll serve as a primary point of contact for regulators and coordinate colleagues across the firm to ensure our responses are clear, accurate, timely, and support constructive regulatory relationships. Additional responsibilities of this role will include:

- Interpreting requests and establishing the scope, responsibilities, and timeline for each examination

- Drafting written submissions and preparing colleagues for meetings with examiners

- Reviewing relevant materials to identify areas for improvement or escalation

- Maintaining examination records and improving the processes we use to manage examinations and related inquiries

About you

- Have 8+ years of relevant legal, compliance, or regulatory experience in financial services, with deep substantive involvement in regulatory examinations

- Have worked directly with the SEC, FINRA, and other regulators at a bank, broker-dealer, trading firm, or similarly regulated financial institution, or advised broker-dealer clients through regulatory examinations as outside counsel

- An excellent writer who can turn complex information into precise, accessible responses

- A polished communicator who can build productive relationships with regulators and handle challenging conversations

- Knowledgeable about the US financial regulatory framework, with the good judgment to recognize when to seek guidance from a subject matter expert

- Highly organized and able to manage deadline-driven work involving contributors from across the firm

- Have a bachelor's degree (having a JD is a plus, though you will not be acting as a lawyer in this role)

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com

postings.title: Sales and Trading
postings.description:
About the Position

As a Sales and Trading intern, you’ll work alongside our experienced Sales people and Sales-Traders, learning how we engage and cover institutional clients on their trading needs in the different asset classes that we cover. They’ll offer insight into the types of client inquiries we handle daily, and you’ll learn how we service our clients, issuers, and prospective clients. The internship is a fast-paced, immersive experience, and you will attend internal classes on various topics where we can teach you the broader fundamentals of finance and trading.

About You

We don’t expect you to have a background in one specific field - we’re looking for smart, driven people who would enjoy working with clients to solve interesting problems. We’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:

- Studying towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, coming into or having completed your final year

- Proactive, reliable, and courteous with strong interpersonal, team working and communication skills

- A self-motivated and entrepreneurial problem-solver who is excited about building relationships with our clients and partners

- A highly analytical and logical thinker, comfortable working with numbers

- Extremely organised with excellent attention to detail

- Interest in learning SQL and/or Python

- Fluent in English, with proficiency in Spanish, Italian, French, Portuguese or German is a plus

Please note: Jane Street will provide flights to and from London as well as accommodation throughout the entirety of the program.
